fields.Name: Model
fields.Description: Root of the model-primitive space: every component that maps assembled features to a prediction, trained or not.
fields.Story: A model component turns evidence into a judgment. Everything below shares one contract — features in, prediction out — however different the internal story.

fields.Name: Linear
fields.Description: Models whose output is a weighted combination of inputs; coefficients are the explanation.
fields.Story: Linear models say exactly why: each input pushes the answer up or down by its weight, and the weights ARE the story.

fields.Name: Logistic Regression
fields.Description: L2-regularized logistic regression for classification; exact per-record contributions from coefficients.
fields.Story: Draws one straight boundary through the feature space and tells you the log-odds contribution of every input.

fields.Name: Ridge Regression
fields.Description: L2-regularized linear regression for numeric targets.
fields.Story: Fits the least-squares line while shrinking weights toward zero, trading a little bias for stability on collinear inputs.

fields.Name: Glass-Box Rubric
fields.Description: Operator-weighted scoring rubric: normalizedScore = scaleMin + (Σ wᵢ·normᵢ / Σ wᵢ) × (scaleMax−scaleMin), with per-input weight modes, caps/floors, and missing-data policy. In given mode the weights are hand-set (no training data needed — a first-class untrainable component); in search mode a constrained non-negative fit proposes them. Ported from Sonar.
fields.Story: The rubric is expertise written down: a human names the signals and how much each should count, and the machine only does the arithmetic — which is why every score it produces can be explained to the person it is about.

fields.Name: Tree Ensemble
fields.Description: Ensembles of decision trees; strong tabular defaults with global feature importance.
fields.Story: Many weak trees vote or correct each other into one strong opinion; the story lives in which features the forest keeps splitting on.

fields.Name: Boosting
fields.Description: Sequential tree ensembles where each tree corrects the residual errors of the ones before.
fields.Story: Boosting is stubbornness as an algorithm: fit, look at what you got wrong, fit the mistake, repeat.

fields.Name: XGBoost
fields.Description: Gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost); the strong accuracy default for tabular problems.
fields.Story: The heavyweight default: regularized boosting that usually wins on tabular data if you give it enough signal and tuning.

fields.Name: LightGBM
fields.Description: Histogram-based leaf-wise gradient boosting; fastest on large/wide data.
fields.Story: Boosting in a hurry — histogram bins and leaf-wise growth make it the choice when the dataset is big and time is not.

fields.Name: Bagging Family
fields.Description: Parallel tree ensembles trained on bootstrap resamples and averaged.
fields.Story: Ask many independently-grown trees and average away their individual noise.

fields.Name: Random Forest
fields.Description: Bootstrap-aggregated decision trees with feature subsampling; robust with minimal tuning.
fields.Story: The forgiving workhorse: hard to overfit badly, hard to configure wrongly, rarely the very best, rarely bad.

fields.Name: Neural
fields.Description: Feed-forward neural networks; best when features are dense/embedding-heavy.
fields.Story: Layers of learned transformations that trade explainability for the ability to bend around structure linear models cannot express.

fields.Name: Multilayer Perceptron
fields.Story: A small dense net — the right tool when embeddings carry the signal and a tree cannot see into them.

fields.Name: Sequence
fields.Description: Models over ORDERED per-entity event sequences (a distinct problem type; ships with the sequence ProblemType widening).
fields.Story: Sequence models care about the order of what happened, not just the totals — trajectories, not snapshots.

fields.Name: Hidden Markov Model
fields.Description: Gaussian HMM: latent regimes with learned transition dynamics over an ordered sequence.
fields.Story: An HMM assumes the visible events are shadows of a few hidden regimes — "engaged", "drifting", "gone" — and learns both the regimes and how members move between them.
